questions.q: Let the position vectors of the vertices $A, B$ and $C$ of a triangle be $2\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}, \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$ and $2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$ respectively. Let ${l}_{1}, {l}_{2}$ and ${l}_{3}$ be the lengths of perpendiculars drawn from the ortho centre of the triangle on the sides $AB, BC$ and $CA$ respectively, then ${l}_{1}^{2} + {l}_{2}^{2} + {l}_{3}^{2}$ equals :
questions.question: Let the position vectors of the vertices $A, B$ and $C$ of a triangle be $2\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}, \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$ and $2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$ respectively. Let ${l}_{1}, {l}_{2}$ and ${l}_{3}$ be the lengths of perpendiculars drawn from the ortho centre of the triangle on the sides $AB, BC$ and $CA$ respectively, then ${l}_{1}^{2} + {l}_{2}^{2} + {l}_{3}^{2}$ equals :
questions.solution:
Given: $A\left(2, 2, 1\right), B\left(1, 2, 2\right)\text{and}C\left(2, 1, 2\right)$ are vertices of $∆ ABC$.

$⇒ AB = \sqrt{\left(2 - 1\right)2 + \left(2 - 2\right)2 + \left(1 - 2\right)2} = \sqrt{2}$

$⇒ BC = \sqrt{\left(1 - 2\right)2 + \left(2 - 1\right)2 + \left(2 - 2\right)2} = \sqrt{2}$

$⇒ CA = \sqrt{\left(2 - 2\right)2 + \left(2 - 1\right)2 + \left(1 - 2\right)2} = \sqrt{2}$

So, $∆ ABC$ is equilateral.

Therefore, orthocentre and centroid will be same.

$⇒ G ≡ \left(\dfrac{2 + 1 + 2}{3}, \dfrac{2 + 2 + 1}{3}, \dfrac{1 + 2 + 2}{3}\right)$

$⇒ G ≡ \left(\dfrac{5}{3}, \dfrac{5}{3}, \dfrac{5}{3}\right)$

Also, mid point of $AB$ is $D\left(\dfrac{3}{2}, 2, \dfrac{3}{2}\right)$

$⇒ {l}_{1} = \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{3}{2} - \dfrac{5}{3}\right)2 + \left(2 - \dfrac{5}{3}\right)2 + \left(\dfrac{3}{2} - \dfrac{5}{3}\right)2}$

$⇒ {l}_{1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{36} + \dfrac{1}{9} + \dfrac{1}{36}}$

$⇒ {l}_{1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{6}}$

Similarly, ${l}_{2} = {l}_{3} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{6}}$

$⇒ \left({l}_{1}\right)2 + \left({l}_{2}\right)2 + \left({l}_{3}\right)2 = \dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{1}{6}$

$⇒ \left({l}_{1}\right)2 + \left({l}_{2}\right)2 + \left({l}_{3}\right)2 = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Given,

$ABCD$ be a quadrilateral. If $E$ and $F$ are the mid points of the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ respectively and $\left(\overset{→}{AB} - \overset{→}{BC}\right) + \left(\overset{→}{AD} - \overset{→}{DC}\right) = k\overset{→}{FE}$,

Now plotting the diagram we get,

Now let position vector of $A, B, C$ and $D$ are $\overset{→}{a,}\overset{→}{b,}\overset{→}{c}$ and $\overset{→}{d}$ respectively

Now by midpoint formula,

Position vector of $E = \dfrac{\overset{→}{OC} + \overset{→}{OA}}{2} = \dfrac{\overset{→}{c} + \overset{→}{a}}{2}$

And Position vector of $F = \dfrac{\overset{→}{b} + \overset{→}{d}}{2}$

Now, $\left(\overset{→}{AB} - \overset{→}{BC}\right) + \overset{→}{AD} - \overset{→}{DC}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{b} - \overset{→}{a} - \left(\overset{→}{c} - \overset{→}{b}\right) + \overset{→}{d} - \overset{→}{a} - \left(\overset{→}{c} - \overset{→}{d}\right)$

$⇒ 2\overset{→}{b} - 2\overset{→}{a} - 2\overset{→}{c} + 2\overset{→}{d}$

$⇒ 2\left(\overset{→}{b} + \overset{→}{d}\right) - 2\left(\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{c}\right)$

$⇒ 4\left[\dfrac{\overset{→}{b} + \overset{→}{d}}{2} - \dfrac{\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{c}}{2}\right] = 4\left[\overset{→}{OF} - \overset{→}{OE}\right]$

If O is the origin and $(\overrightarrow{\mathrm{OQ}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{OA}})-\frac{1}{5}|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{OP}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{OA}}|^2=10$, then the value of r is :
questions.question: Let the point A divide the line segment joining the points $P(-1,-1,2)$ and $Q(5,5,10)$ internally in the ratio $\mathrm{r}: 1(\mathrm{r}\gt0)$. If O is the origin and $(\overrightarrow{\mathrm{OQ}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{OA}})-\frac{1}{5}|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{OP}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{OA}}|^2=10$, then the value of r is :
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & A=\left(\frac{5 r-1}{r+1}, \frac{5 r-1}{r+1}, \frac{10 r+2}{r+1}\right) \\ & (\overrightarrow{O Q} \cdot \overrightarrow{O A})-\frac{1}{5}|\overrightarrow{O P} \times \overrightarrow{O A}|^2=10 \\ & \overrightarrow{O Q}=5 \hat{i}+5 \hat{j}+10 \hat{k} \\ & \overrightarrow{O A}=\frac{5 r-1}{r+1} \hat{i}+\frac{5 r-1}{r+1} \hat{j}+\frac{10 r+2}{r+1} \hat{k} \\ & \overrightarrow{O P}=-\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2 \hat{k} \\ & \left.\overrightarrow{O P} \times \overrightarrow{O A}=\frac{1}{r+1} \right\rvert\, \frac{5 r-1}{5} \quad 5 r-1 \quad 10 r+2 \\ & =\frac{1}{r+1}(\hat{i}(20 r)-\hat{j}(20 r)) \\ & =5\left(\frac{5 r-1}{r+1}\right)+5\left(\frac{5 r-1}{r+1}\right)+10\left(\frac{10 r+2}{r+1}\right) \\ & \quad-\frac{1}{5}\left(\frac{2 \times 400 r^2}{(r+1)^2}\right)=10 \\ & \frac{150 r+10}{r+1}-\frac{1}{5}\left(\frac{2 \times 400 r^2}{(r+1)^2}\right)=10 \\ & (150 r+10)(r+1)-160 r^2=10(r+1)^2 \\ & (15 r+1)(r+1)-16 r^2=(r+1)^2 \\ & 15 r^2+16 r+1-16 r^2=r^2+2 r+1 \\ & -2 r^2+14 r=0\end{aligned}$ $r=0,7$

questions.q: Let the position vectors of three vertices of a triangle be $4 \vec{p}+\vec{q}-3 \vec{r},-5 \vec{p}+\vec{q}+2 \vec{r}$ and $2 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{p}}-\overrightarrow{\mathrm{q}}+2 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{r}}$. If the position vectors of the orthocenter and the circumcenter of the triangle are $\frac{\vec{p}+\vec{q}+\vec{r}}{4}$ and $\alpha \vec{p}+\beta \vec{q}+\gamma \vec{r}$ respectively, then $\alpha+2 \beta+5 \gamma$ is equal to :
questions.question: Let the position vectors of three vertices of a triangle be $4 \vec{p}+\vec{q}-3 \vec{r},-5 \vec{p}+\vec{q}+2 \vec{r}$ and $2 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{p}}-\overrightarrow{\mathrm{q}}+2 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{r}}$. If the position vectors of the orthocenter and the circumcenter of the triangle are $\frac{\vec{p}+\vec{q}+\vec{r}}{4}$ and $\alpha \vec{p}+\beta \vec{q}+\gamma \vec{r}$ respectively, then $\alpha+2 \beta+5 \gamma$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
We know that
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{O}\text { (orthocentre) } \frac{\overrightarrow{\mathrm{p}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{q}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{r}}}{4} \\ & \mathrm{C}(\text { circum centre) } \alpha \overrightarrow{\mathrm{p}}+\beta \overrightarrow{\mathrm{q}}+\gamma \overrightarrow{\mathrm{r}} \\ & \mathrm{C} \text { (centroid) }=\frac{\overrightarrow{\mathrm{p}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{q}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{r}}}{3} \end{aligned}$ by relation $\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 2(\alpha \overrightarrow{\mathrm{p}}+\beta \overrightarrow{\mathrm{q}}+\gamma \overrightarrow{\mathrm{r}})+\frac{\overrightarrow{\mathrm{p}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{q}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{r}}}{4}=3\left(\frac{\overrightarrow{\mathrm{p}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{q}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{r}}}{3}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow 8(\alpha \overrightarrow{\mathrm{p}}+\beta \overrightarrow{\mathrm{q}}+\gamma \overrightarrow{\mathrm{r}})=3(\overrightarrow{\mathrm{p}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{q}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{r}}) \\ & \Rightarrow 8 \alpha=3,8 \beta=3,8 \gamma=3 \\ & \alpha=\frac{3}{8}, \beta=\frac{3}{8}, \gamma=\frac{3}{8} \\ & \therefore \alpha+2 \beta+3 \gamma \\ & \frac{3}{8}+\frac{6}{8}+\frac{15}{8}=\frac{24}{8}=3 \end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $P$ be a point in the plane of the vectors $\overrightarrow{A B}=3 \hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ and $\overrightarrow{A C}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}+3 \hat{k}$ such that $P$ is equidistant from the lines AB and AC. If $|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{AP}}|=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}$, then the area of the triangle ABP is:
questions.question: Let $P$ be a point in the plane of the vectors $\overrightarrow{A B}=3 \hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ and $\overrightarrow{A C}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}+3 \hat{k}$ such that $P$ is equidistant from the lines AB and AC. If $|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{AP}}|=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}$, then the area of the triangle ABP is:
questions.solution:
Since P is equidistant from lines AB and AC through point A, it lies along the angle bisector direction. The unit vectors are $\hat{u}_{AB} = \frac{3\vec{i} + \vec{j} - \vec{k}}{\sqrt{11}}$ and $\hat{u}_{AC} = \frac{\vec{i} - \vec{j} + 3\vec{k}}{\sqrt{11}}$.
The bisector direction is proportional to $2\vec{i} + \vec{k}$, so $\vec{AP} = \lambda(2\vec{i} + \vec{k})$.
From $|\vec{AP}| = \frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}$: $|\lambda|\sqrt{5} = \frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}$, giving $\lambda = \frac{1}{2}$.
Thus $\vec{AP} = \vec{i} + \frac{1}{2}\vec{k}$.
Area of triangle ABP = $\frac{1}{2}|\vec{AB} \times \vec{AP}|$.
Computing: $\vec{AB} \times \vec{AP} = \frac{1}{2}\vec{i} - \frac{5}{2}\vec{j} - \vec{k}$.
$|\vec{AB} \times \vec{AP}| = \sqrt{\frac{1}{4} + \frac{25}{4} + 1} = \sqrt{\frac{30}{4}} = \frac{\sqrt{30}}{2}$.
Area = $\frac{\sqrt{30}}{4}$.

questions.q: Let $\hat{u}$ and $\hat{v}$ be unit vectors inclined at an acute angle such that $|\hat{u}\times\hat{v}|=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$. If $\vec{A}=\lambda\hat{u}+\hat{v}+(\hat{u}\times\hat{v})$, then $\lambda$ is equal to:
questions.question: Let $\hat{u}$ and $\hat{v}$ be unit vectors inclined at an acute angle such that $|\hat{u}\times\hat{v}|=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$. If $\vec{A}=\lambda\hat{u}+\hat{v}+(\hat{u}\times\hat{v})$, then $\lambda$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given $|\hat{u}\times\hat{v}| = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ and $\hat{u}, \hat{v}$ are unit vectors.

$\sin\theta = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

Since the angle $\theta$ is acute, $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$.

$\hat{u}\cdot\hat{v} = \cos\dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Given $\vec{A} = \lambda\hat{u} + \hat{v} + (\hat{u}\times\hat{v})$.

Taking the dot product with $\hat{u}$:

$\vec{A}\cdot\hat{u} = \lambda(\hat{u}\cdot\hat{u}) + \hat{v}\cdot\hat{u} + (\hat{u}\times\hat{v})\cdot\hat{u}$

$\vec{A}\cdot\hat{u} = \lambda(1) + \dfrac{1}{2} + 0 = \lambda + \dfrac{1}{2}$

Taking the dot product with $\hat{v}$:

$\vec{A}\cdot\hat{v} = \lambda(\hat{u}\cdot\hat{v}) + \hat{v}\cdot\hat{v} + (\hat{u}\times\hat{v})\cdot\hat{v}$

$\vec{A}\cdot\hat{v} = \lambda\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) + 1 + 0 = \dfrac{\lambda}{2} + 1$

From the first equation, we have $1 = 2(\vec{A}\cdot\hat{u}) - 2\lambda$.

Substituting this into the second equation:

$\vec{A}\cdot\hat{v} = \dfrac{\lambda}{2} + 2(\vec{A}\cdot\hat{u}) - 2\lambda$

$\vec{A}\cdot\hat{v} = 2(\vec{A}\cdot\hat{u}) - \dfrac{3\lambda}{2}$

$\dfrac{3\lambda}{2} = 2(\vec{A}\cdot\hat{u}) - (\vec{A}\cdot\hat{v})$

$\lambda = \dfrac{4}{3}(\vec{A}\cdot\hat{u}) - \dfrac{2}{3}(\vec{A}\cdot\hat{v})$

Answer: $\dfrac{4}{3}(\vec{A}\cdot\hat{u})-\dfrac{2}{3}(\vec{A}\cdot\hat{v})$

questions.q: Two adjacent sides of a parallelogram PQRS are given by $\vec{PQ} = \hat{j} + \hat{k}$ and $\vec{PS} = \hat{i} - \hat{j}$. If the side PS is rotated about the point P by an acute angle $\alpha$ in the plane of the parallelogram so that it becomes perpendicular to the side PQ, then $\sin^2\left(\dfrac{5\alpha}{2}\right) - \sin^2\left(\dfrac{\alpha}{2}\right)$ is equal to:
questions.question: Two adjacent sides of a parallelogram PQRS are given by $\vec{PQ} = \hat{j} + \hat{k}$ and $\vec{PS} = \hat{i} - \hat{j}$. If the side PS is rotated about the point P by an acute angle $\alpha$ in the plane of the parallelogram so that it becomes perpendicular to the side PQ, then $\sin^2\left(\dfrac{5\alpha}{2}\right) - \sin^2\left(\dfrac{\alpha}{2}\right)$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Let $\theta$ be the angle between the vectors $\vec{PQ}$ and $\vec{PS}$.

$\cos \theta = \dfrac{\vec{PQ} \cdot \vec{PS}}{|\vec{PQ}| |\vec{PS}|}$

$\cos \theta = \dfrac{(\hat{j} + \hat{k}) \cdot (\hat{i} - \hat{j})}{\sqrt{1^2 + 1^2} \sqrt{1^2 + (-1)^2}}$

$\cos \theta = \dfrac{-1}{\sqrt{2} \times \sqrt{2}} = -\dfrac{1}{2}$

$\theta = 120^{\circ}$

The side PS is rotated by an acute angle $\alpha$ in the plane of the parallelogram to become perpendicular to PQ. The new angle between the sides is $90^{\circ}$.

$\alpha = 120^{\circ} - 90^{\circ} = 30^{\circ}$

The given expression is $\sin^2\left(\dfrac{5\alpha}{2}\right) - \sin^2\left(\dfrac{\alpha}{2}\right)$.

Using the trigonometric identity $\sin^2 A - \sin^2 B = \sin(A+B) \sin(A-B)$:

$\sin^2\left(\dfrac{5\alpha}{2}\right) - \sin^2\left(\dfrac{\alpha}{2}\right) = \sin\left(\dfrac{5\alpha}{2} + \dfrac{\alpha}{2}\right) \sin\left(\dfrac{5\alpha}{2} - \dfrac{\alpha}{2}\right)$

$= \sin(3\alpha) \sin(2\alpha)$

Substituting $\alpha = 30^{\circ}$:

$= \sin(90^{\circ}) \sin(60^{\circ})$

$= 1 \times \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

Let $ABC$ be a triangle such that $\overset{→}{BC} = \overset{→}{a}, \overset{→}{CA} = \overset{→}{b}$, $\overset{→}{AB} = \overset{→}{c}, \left|\overset{→}{a}\right| = 6\sqrt{2}, \left|\overset{→}{b}\right| = 2\sqrt{3}$ and $\overset{→}{b} \cdot \overset{→}{c} = 12$ Consider the statements :

$\left(S1\right)$: $\left|\left(\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right) + \left(\overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{b}\right)\right| - \left|\overset{→}{c}\right| = 6\left(2\sqrt{2} - 1\right)$

questions.solution:
We know that by triangle law of vector addition,

$\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b} + \overset{→}{c} = 0$

$⇒ \overset{→}{b} + \overset{→}{c} = - \overset{→}{a}$

Squaring both side we get,

$\left|\overset{→}{b}\right|2 + \left|\overset{→}{c}\right|2 + 2\overset{→}{b} \cdot \overset{→}{c} = \left|\overset{→}{a}\right|2$

Now putting the given value $\left|\overset{→}{a}\right| = 6\sqrt{2}, \left|\overset{→}{b}\right| = 2\sqrt{3} \text{ and } \overset{→}{b} . \overset{→}{c} = 12$

We get, $\left|\overset{→}{c}\right|2 = 36$

So, $\left|\overset{→}{c}\right| = 6$

Now, $S1: \left|\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} + \overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{b}\right| - \left|\overset{→}{c}\right|$

$⇒ \left|\left(\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{c}\right) \times \overset{→}{b}\right| - \left|\overset{→}{c}\right|$

$⇒ 0 - 6 = - 6$

And $S2: \overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b} + \overset{→}{c} = 0$

$\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b} = - \overset{→}{c}$

Squaring both side we get,

$\left|\overset{→}{a}\right|2 + \left|\overset{→}{b}\right|2 - 2\left|\overset{→}{a}\right|\left|\overset{→}{b}\right|cos\left(∠ ACB\right) = \left|\overset{→}{c}\right|2$

$⇒ 72 + 12 - 24\sqrt{6}cos\left(∠ ACB\right) = 36$

$⇒ cos\left(∠ ACB\right) = \dfrac{48}{24\sqrt{6}} = \dfrac{2}{6} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}$

questions.question: If $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ are two vectors such that $|\vec{a}| = 2$ and $|\vec{b}| = 3$, then the maximum value of $3\left|\left(3\vec{a} + 2\vec{b}\right)\right| + 4\left|\left(3\vec{a} - 2\vec{b}\right)\right|$ is :
questions.solution:
Let $\theta$ be the angle between $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$.

We have $|3\vec{a} + 2\vec{b}| = \sqrt{9|\vec{a}|^2 + 4|\vec{b}|^2 + 12|\vec{a}||\vec{b}|\cos\theta}$

Substituting $|\vec{a}| = 2$ and $|\vec{b}| = 3$:

$|3\vec{a} + 2\vec{b}| = \sqrt{9(4) + 4(9) + 12(2)(3)\cos\theta} = \sqrt{36 + 36 + 72\cos\theta}$

$|3\vec{a} + 2\vec{b}| = \sqrt{72(1+\cos\theta)} = \sqrt{144\cos^2\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)} = 12\cos\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)$

Similarly, $|3\vec{a} - 2\vec{b}| = \sqrt{9|\vec{a}|^2 + 4|\vec{b}|^2 - 12|\vec{a}||\vec{b}|\cos\theta}$

$|3\vec{a} - 2\vec{b}| = \sqrt{36 + 36 - 72\cos\theta} = \sqrt{72(1-\cos\theta)} = \sqrt{144\sin^2\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)} = 12\sin\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)$

The given expression becomes:

$3|3\vec{a} + 2\vec{b}| + 4|3\vec{a} - 2\vec{b}| = 3\left(12\cos\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)\right) + 4\left(12\sin\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)\right)$

$= 36\cos\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right) + 48\sin\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)$

The maximum value of $A\cos x + B\sin x$ is $\sqrt{A^2 + B^2}$.

Maximum value $= \sqrt{36^2 + 48^2} = \sqrt{1296 + 2304} = \sqrt{3600} = 60$

Answer: $60$

Let $a$ and $b$ be two unit vectors such that $\left|\left(a + b\right) + 2\left(a \times b\right)\right| = 2$. If $\theta \in \left(0, \pi\right)$ is the angle between $\overset{^}{a}$ and $\overset{^}{b}$, then among the statements:
$\left(S1\right): 2\left|\overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b}\right| = \left|\overset{^}{a} - \overset{^}{b}\right|$
$\left(S2\right)$ : The projection of $\overset{^}{a}$ on $\left(\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right)$ is $\dfrac{1}{2}$
questions.question:
Let $a$ and $b$ be two unit vectors such that $\left|\left(a + b\right) + 2\left(a \times b\right)\right| = 2$. If $\theta \in \left(0, \pi\right)$ is the angle between $\overset{^}{a}$ and $\overset{^}{b}$, then among the statements:
$\left(S1\right): 2\left|\overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b}\right| = \left|\overset{^}{a} - \overset{^}{b}\right|$
$\left(S2\right)$ : The projection of $\overset{^}{a}$ on $\left(\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right)$ is $\dfrac{1}{2}$
questions.solution:
Given,

$\left|\left(\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right) + 2\left(\overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b}\right)\right| = 2, \theta \in \left(0, \pi\right)$

Squaring both side we get,

$\left(\left(\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right) + 2\left(\overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b}\right)\right) \cdot \left(\left(\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right) + 2\left(\overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b}\right)\right) = 4$

$\left|\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right|2 + 4\left|\left(\overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b}\right)\right|2 + 0 = 4$

Let the angle be $\theta$ between $\overset{^}{a}$ and $\overset{^}{b}$

$⇒ \left|\overset{^}{a}\right|2 + \left|\overset{^}{b}\right|2 + 2\left|\overset{^}{a}\right|\left|\overset{^}{b}\right|cos\theta + 4\left(\left|\overset{^}{a}\right|\left|\overset{^}{b}\right|sin\theta\right) = 4$

$⇒ 2 + 2cos\theta + 4{sin}^{2}\theta = 4$

$⇒ 2 + 2cos\theta - 4{cos}^{2}\theta = 0$

Let $cos\theta = t$ then

$⇒ 2{t}^{2} - t - 1 = 0$

$⇒ 2{t}^{2} - 2t + t - 1 = 0$

$⇒ 2t\left(t - 1\right) + \left(t - 1\right) = 0$

$\left(2t + 1\right)\left(t - 1\right) = 0$

So, $t = - \dfrac{1}{2}$ or $t = 1$

Then, $cos\theta = - \dfrac{1}{2}$ or $cos\theta = 1$ which is not possible as $0 \in \left(0, \pi\right)$

So, $\theta = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$

Now,

${S}_{1} ⇒ 2\left|a \times b\right| = 2sin\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right) = 2 \times \dfrac{3}{2} = \sqrt{3}$

And $\left|\overset{^}{a} - \overset{^}{b}\right| = \sqrt{1 + 1 - 2cos\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)}$

$= \sqrt{2 - 2 \times \left(- \dfrac{1}{2}\right)}$

$= \sqrt{3}$

${S}_{1}$ is correct.

${S}_{2}$ projection of $\overset{^}{a}$ on $\left(\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{\overset{^}{a} . \left(\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right)}{∣ \overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b} )} = \dfrac{1 + cos\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)}{2 + 2cos\dfrac{2\pi}{3}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1 - \dfrac{1}{2}}{1} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Which is true, So both are true.

questions.q: Let $\overset{→}{a} = \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$ and let $\overset{→}{b}$ be a vector such that $\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} = 2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b} = 3$. Then the projection of $\overset{→}{b}$ on the vector $\overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b}$ is:
questions.question: Let $\overset{→}{a} = \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$ and let $\overset{→}{b}$ be a vector such that $\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} = 2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b} = 3$. Then the projection of $\overset{→}{b}$ on the vector $\overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b}$ is:
questions.solution:
Given,

$\overset{→}{a} = \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$ , $\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} = 2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b} = 3$

Now using the formula $\left|\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right|2 + \left|\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b}\right|2 = \left(\left|\overset{→}{a}\right|2 \cdot \left|\overset{→}{b}\right|2{sin}^{2}\theta + \left|\overset{→}{a}\right|2 \cdot \left|\overset{→}{b}\right|2{cos}^{2}\theta\right)$

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right|2 + \left|\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b}\right|2 = \left|\overset{→}{a}\right|2 \cdot \left|\overset{→}{b}\right|2\left({sin}^{2}\theta + {cos}^{2}\theta\right) = \left|\overset{→}{a}\right|2 \cdot \left|\overset{→}{b}\right|2$

We get,

$⇒ \left|2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{k}\right|2 + \left|3\right|2 = \left|\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right|2\left|\overset{→}{b}\right|2$

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{b}\right|2 = \dfrac{5 + 9}{6} = \dfrac{14}{6} = \dfrac{7}{3}$

Now finding $\left|\overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b}\right| = \sqrt{\left|\overset{→}{a}\right|2 + \left|\overset{→}{b}\right|2 - 2\left|\overset{→}{a}\right|\left|\overset{→}{b}\right|} = \sqrt{6 + \dfrac{7}{3} - 6} = \sqrt{\dfrac{7}{3}}$

Now projection of $\overset{→}{b}$ on $\overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b} = \overset{→}{b} \cdot \left(\overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b}\right)\left|\overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b}\right|$

$= \overset{→}{b} \cdot \overset{→}{a} - \left|\overset{→}{b}\right|2\left|\overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b}\right| = \dfrac{3 - \dfrac{7}{3}}{\dfrac{7}{3}}$

$= \dfrac{2}{21}$

questions.question: Let $\vec{c}$ be the projection vector of $\vec{b}=\lambda \hat{i}+4 \hat{k}, \lambda\gt0$, on the vector $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+2 \hat{k}$. If $|\vec{a}+\vec{c}|=7$, then the area of the parallelogram formed by the vectors $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ is ________
questions.solution:
$\vec{c}=\left(\frac{\vec{b} \cdot \vec{a}}{|\vec{b}|}\right) \frac{\vec{a}}{|\vec{a}|}$
$\begin{aligned} & \quad=\left(\frac{\lambda+8}{9}\right)(\hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+2 \hat{k}) \\ & |\vec{a}+\vec{c}|=7 \\ & \left.\Rightarrow\left(\frac{\lambda+8}{9}+1\right) \hat{i}+\left(\frac{2(\lambda+8)}{9}+2\right) \hat{j}+\left(\frac{2(\lambda+8)}{9}+2\right) \hat{k} \right\rvert\,=7 \\ & \left(\frac{\lambda+8}{9}+1\right)^2+\left(\frac{2(\lambda+8)}{9}+2\right)^2+\left(\frac{2(\lambda+8)}{9}+2\right)^2=49\end{aligned}$
$\Rightarrow \lambda=4 \Rightarrow \vec{c}=\frac{4}{3} \hat{i}+\frac{8}{3} \hat{j}+\frac{8}{3} \hat{k}$

So,

Then,

$\overset{→}{c} \cdot ( \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} ) + 25 = 0$

$⇒ 15x - 20y - 25z + 25 = 0$

$⇒ 3x - 4y - 5z = - 5 . . . \left(1\right)$

Also,

$\overset{→}{c} \cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right) = 4$

$⇒ x + y + z = 4 . . . . \left(2\right)$

And projection of $\overset{→}{c}$ on $\overset{→}{a}$ is

$\dfrac{\overset{→}{c} \cdot \overset{→}{a}}{| \overset{→}{a} |} = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(x\overset{^}{i} + y\overset{^}{j} + z\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j}\right)}{16 + 9} = 1$

$⇒ 4x + 3y = 5 . . . . \left(3\right)$

Solving $\left(1\right), \left(2\right) \text{ and } \left(3\right)$, we get

$x = 2, y = - 1, z = 3$

So,

$\overset{→}{c} = 2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$

Projection of $\overset{→}{c}$ on $\overset{→}{b}$ is

$\overset{→}{b} = 3\overset{^}{i} - 4\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}$

So,

$\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} \text{ and } \overset{^}{j} \text{ and } \overset{^}{k} \\ 4 \text{ and } 3 \text{ and } 0 \\ 3 \text{ and } - 4 \text{ and } 5\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} = 15\overset{^}{i} - 20\overset{^}{j} - 25\overset{^}{k}$

Then,

$\overset{→}{c} \cdot ( \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} ) + 25 = 0$

$⇒ 15x - 20y - 25z + 25 = 0$

$⇒ 3x - 4y - 5z = - 5 . . . \left(1\right)$

Also,

$\overset{→}{c} \cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right) = 4$

$⇒ x + y + z = 4 . . . . \left(2\right)$

$x = 2, y = - 1, z = 3$

$\overset{→}{c} = 2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$

Projection of $\overset{→}{c}$ on $\overset{→}{b}$ is

questions.solution:
Given,

A triangle $ABC$

$\overset{→}{CA} = 4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + \delta\overset{^}{k}$

Now plotting the diagram we get,

Now from triangle law of addition we get,

$\overset{→}{CA} + \overset{→}{AB} = \overset{→}{CB}$

$⇒ 4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + \delta\overset{^}{k} + \left(- 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right) = \alpha\overset{^}{i} + \beta\overset{^}{j} + \gamma\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ 2\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} + \left(\delta + 3\right)\overset{^}{k} = \alpha\overset{^}{i} + \beta\overset{^}{j} + \gamma\overset{^}{k}$

Now on comparing both side we get,

$\alpha = 2, \beta = 4 \text{ and } \gamma = \delta + 3$

Now area of triangle is given by,

$A = \dfrac{1}{2}\left|\overset{→}{AB} \times \overset{→}{BC}\right|$

$⇒ 5\sqrt{6} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} \text{ and } \overset{^}{j} \text{ and } \overset{^}{k} \\ - 2 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } 3 \\ 2 \text{ and } 4 \text{ and } \gamma\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \left(5\sqrt{6}\right)2 = \left(\gamma - 12\right)2 + \left(6 + 2\gamma\right)2 + 100$

$⇒ 5{γ}^{2} = 320$

$⇒ {γ}^{2} = 64 ⇒ \gamma = 8$

So, $\delta = 8 - 3 = 5$

$\overset{→}{CB} \cdot \overset{→}{CA} = \left(\alpha\overset{^}{i} + \beta\overset{^}{j} + \gamma\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + \delta\overset{^}{k}\right)$

$⇒ \overset{→}{CB} \cdot \overset{→}{CA} = \left(2\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} + 8\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}\right) = 8 + 12 + 40 = 60$

questions.solution:
Given,

$\overset{→}{a} = 2\overset{^}{i} + 7\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}, \overset{^}{b} = 3\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{c} = \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$

And $\overset{→}{d}$ be a vector which is perpendicular to both $\overset{→}{a}$ and $\overset{→}{b}$,

So, $\overset{→}{d} = \lambda\left(\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right)$

Now finding, $\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} \text{ and } \overset{^}{j} \text{ and } \overset{^}{k} \\ 2 \text{ and } 7 \text{ and } - 1 \\ 3 \text{ and } 0 \text{ and } 5\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} = 35\overset{^}{i} - 13\overset{^}{j} - 21\overset{^}{k}$

So, $\overset{→}{d} = \lambda\left(35\overset{^}{i} - 13\overset{^}{j} - 21\overset{^}{k}\right)$

Also given,

$\overset{→}{c} \cdot \overset{→}{d} = 12$

$⇒ \overset{→}{c} \cdot \overset{→}{d} = \left(\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \lambda\left(35\overset{^}{i} - 13\overset{^}{j} - 21\overset{^}{k}\right)$

$⇒ \lambda ( 35 + 13 - 42 ) = 12$

$⇒ \lambda = 2$

So, $\overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{d} = 2 \times \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} \text{ and } \overset{^}{j} \text{ and } \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 \text{ and } - 1 \text{ and } 2 \\ 35 \text{ and } - 13 \text{ and } - 21\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{d} = 2\left(47\overset{^}{i} + 91\overset{^}{j} + 22\overset{^}{k}\right)$

Now finding,

$\left(- \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{d}\right) = 2\left(- \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right)\left(47\overset{^}{i} + 91\overset{^}{j} + 22\overset{^}{k}\right)$

$⇒ \left(- \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{d}\right) = 2\left(- 47 + 91 - 22\right) = 44$

questions.solution:
Given,

$\overset{→}{a}$ be a non-zero vector parallel to the line of intersection of the two planes described by $\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}, \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}$,

So finding the normal vector to the above plane, we get,

$\overset{→}{n}1 = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} \text{ and } \overset{^}{j} \text{ and } \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } 0 \\ 1 \text{ and } 0 \text{ and } 1\end{cases}\right| = \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$

And normal vector to planes $\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j}, \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$ will be,

$\overset{→}{n}2 = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} \text{ and } \overset{^}{j} \text{ and } \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 \text{ and } - 1 \text{ and } 0 \\ 0 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } - 1\end{cases}\right| = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

Now $\overset{→}{a} = \lambda\left(\overset{→}{n}1 \times \overset{→}{n}2\right)$

So, direction ratio of $\overset{→}{a} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} \text{ and } \overset{^}{j} \text{ and } \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 \text{ and } - 1 \text{ and } - 1 \\ 1 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } 1\end{cases}\right|$$= - 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$

Hence, direction ratio of $\overset{→}{a} = \left(0, - 2, 2\right) = \left(0, - 1, 1\right)$

Now given, $\overset{→}{b} = 2\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

And $\overset{→}{a} = \lambda ( - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k} )$

So, $\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b} = 6 = \lambda ( 2 + 1 )$

$⇒ \lambda = 2$

$∴ \overset{→}{a} = - 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$

Now we know that, $\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b} = | \overset{¯}{a} | | b | cos\theta$

$⇒ 6 = 2\sqrt{2} \times 3cos\theta$

$⇒ cos\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ \theta = \dfrac{π}{4}$

Now finding, $\left|\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right| = \left|\overset{→}{a}\right|\left|\overset{→}{b}\right|sin\theta = 2\sqrt{2} \times 3 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 6$

Hence, ordered pair $\left(\theta, \left|\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right|\right) = \left(\dfrac{π}{4}, 6\right)$

questions.question: Let $\overset{→}{a} = 3\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{c} = 2\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k} .$ If $\overset{→}{b}$ is a vector such that $\overset{→}{a} = \overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c}$ and $| \overset{→}{b}{|}^{2} = 50,$ then $\left|72 - \left|\overset{→}{b} + \overset{→}{c}\right|2\right|$ is equal to $__________ .$
questions.solution:
Given,

$\overset{→}{a} = 3\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{c} = 2\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k} .$

And $\overset{→}{b}$ is a vector such that $\overset{→}{a} = \overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c}$ and $| \overset{→}{b}{|}^{2} = 50,$

Now solving, $| \overset{→}{a} | = | \overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c} |$

$⇒ \sqrt{{3}^{2} + {1}^{2} + {1}^{2}} = | \overset{→}{b} | \cdot \sqrt{{2}^{2} + {3}^{2} + {3}^{2}} \cdot sin\theta$

$⇒ \sqrt{11} = \sqrt{50} \cdot \sqrt{22} \cdot sin\theta$

$∴ sin\theta = \dfrac{1}{10}$ or $cos\theta = \dfrac{99}{10}$

Now solving,$\left|72 - \left|\overset{→}{b} + \overset{→}{c}\right|2\right|$ we get,

$\left|72 - \left|\overset{→}{b} + \overset{→}{c}\right|2\right|$

$= \left|72 - \left(\left|\overset{→}{b}\right|2 + \left|\overset{→}{c}\right|2 + 2\left|\overset{→}{b}\right|\left|\overset{→}{c}\right|cos\theta\right)\right|$

$= \left|72 - \left(50 + 22 + 2 \times 5\sqrt{2} . \sqrt{22}\dfrac{99}{10}\right)\right|$

$= \left|72 - \left(72 + \dfrac{2 \times 5 \times 2 \times 11 \times 3}{10}\right\right|$

$= \left|66\right| = 66$

questions.question: Let three vectors $\overset{→}{a}, \overset{→}{b}$ and $\overset{→}{c}$ be such that $\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} = \overset{→}{c}, \overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c} = \overset{→}{a}$ and $| \overset{→}{a} | = 2 .$ Then which one of the following is not true?
questions.solution:
The first option is $\overset{→}{a} \times \left(\left(\overset{→}{b} + \overset{→}{c}\right) \times \left(\overset{→}{b} - \overset{→}{c}\right)\right)$

$= \overset{→}{a} \times \left(\left(\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{b} - \overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c} + \overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{b} - \overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{c}\right)\right)$

But, we know that $\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{b} = 0 = \overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{c}$

$= \overset{→}{a} \times \left(\overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{b} - \overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c}\right)$

Given, $\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c} = \overset{→}{a}, ⇒ \overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{b} = - \overset{→}{a}$

$= \overset{→}{a} \times \left(- \overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c}\right)$

$= \left(- \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{a}\right) - \left(\overset{→}{a} \times \left(\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c}\right)\right)$

$= 0 - \left(\overset{→}{a} \times \left(\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c}\right)\right) = - \left(\overset{→}{a} \times \left(\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c}\right)\right)$

$= - ( \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{a} ) = \overset{→}{0}$

$∵ \overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c} = \overset{→}{a}$

Hence, the option $\left(A\right)$ is correct.

For the second option, we have

Projection of $\overset{→}{a}$ on $\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c}$ is

$= \dfrac{\overset{→}{a} \cdot ( \overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c} )}{| \overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c} |} = \dfrac{\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{a}}{| \overset{→}{a} |}$

Using, $\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{a} = \left|\overset{→}{a}\right|2,$ we get

$= \left|\overset{→}{a}\right|2\left|\overset{→}{a}\right| = \left|\overset{→}{a}\right| = 2 .$

Hence, the option $\left(B\right)$ is correct.

For the third option, we have $\left[\begin{cases}\overset{→}{a} \text{ and } \overset{→}{b} \text{ and } \overset{→}{c}\end{cases}\right] + \left[\begin{cases}\overset{→}{c} \text{ and } \overset{→}{a} \text{ and } \overset{→}{b}\end{cases}\right]$

We know that $\left[\begin{cases}\overset{→}{a} \text{ and } \overset{→}{b} \text{ and } \overset{→}{c}\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}\overset{→}{c} \text{ and } \overset{→}{a} \text{ and } \overset{→}{b}\end{cases}\right],$ and $\left[\begin{cases}\overset{→}{a} \text{ and } \overset{→}{b} \text{ and } \overset{→}{c}\end{cases}\right] = \overset{→}{a} \cdot ( \overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c} ) ,$

$⇒ \left[\begin{cases}\overset{→}{a} \text{ and } \overset{→}{b} \text{ and } \overset{→}{c}\end{cases}\right] + \left[\begin{cases}\overset{→}{c} \text{ and } \overset{→}{a} \text{ and } \overset{→}{b}\end{cases}\right] = 2\left[\begin{cases}\overset{→}{a} \text{ and } \overset{→}{b} \text{ and } \overset{→}{c}\end{cases}\right] = 2\overset{→}{a} \cdot ( \overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c} )$

$= 2\left(\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{a}\right) = 2 | \overset{→}{a}{|}^{2} = 2 \times {2}^{2} = 8 .$

Hence, the option $\left(C\right)$ is correct.

$(\vec{c} + \vec{d}) \cdot (-7\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}) = \pm(-14 + 6 + 12) = \pm 4$.

Coeff of $xy = 0$: $K^2 - 5K + 4 = 0 \Rightarrow K = 1, 4$.

questions.q: Let $\vec{a} = \sqrt{7}\hat{i} + \hat{j} - \hat{k}$ and $\vec{b} = \hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$. If $\vec{r}$ is a vector such that $\vec{r} \times \vec{a} + \vec{a} \times \vec{b} = \vec{0}$ and $\vec{r} \cdot \vec{a} = 0$, then $|3\vec{r}|^2$ is equal to:
questions.question: Let $\vec{a} = \sqrt{7}\hat{i} + \hat{j} - \hat{k}$ and $\vec{b} = \hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$. If $\vec{r}$ is a vector such that $\vec{r} \times \vec{a} + \vec{a} \times \vec{b} = \vec{0}$ and $\vec{r} \cdot \vec{a} = 0$, then $|3\vec{r}|^2$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given $\vec{r} \times \vec{a} + \vec{a} \times \vec{b} = \vec{0}$

$\Rightarrow \vec{r} \times \vec{a} - \vec{b} \times \vec{a} = \vec{0}$

$\Rightarrow (\vec{r} - \vec{b}) \times \vec{a} = \vec{0}$

$\Rightarrow \vec{r} - \vec{b} = \lambda \vec{a}$

$\Rightarrow \vec{r} = \vec{b} + \lambda \vec{a}$

Taking dot product with $\vec{a}$ on both sides:

$\vec{r} \cdot \vec{a} = \vec{b} \cdot \vec{a} + \lambda |\vec{a}|^2$

Since $\vec{r} \cdot \vec{a} = 0$, we get:

$\lambda = -\dfrac{\vec{b} \cdot \vec{a}}{|\vec{a}|^2}$

We have $\vec{a} = \sqrt{7}\hat{i} + \hat{j} - \hat{k}$ and $\vec{b} = \hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$.

$\vec{b} \cdot \vec{a} = (0)(\sqrt{7}) + (1)(1) + (2)(-1) = -1$

$|\vec{a}|^2 = (\sqrt{7})^2 + (1)^2 + (-1)^2 = 9$

$|\vec{b}|^2 = (1)^2 + (2)^2 = 5$

Substituting these values:

$\lambda = -\dfrac{-1}{9} = \dfrac{1}{9}$

Therefore, $\vec{r} = \vec{b} + \dfrac{1}{9}\vec{a}$

Squaring both sides:

$|\vec{r}|^2 = |\vec{b}|^2 + \dfrac{1}{81}|\vec{a}|^2 + \dfrac{2}{9}(\vec{b} \cdot \vec{a})$

$|\vec{r}|^2 = 5 + \dfrac{1}{81}(9) + \dfrac{2}{9}(-1)$

$|\vec{r}|^2 = 5 + \dfrac{1}{9} - \dfrac{2}{9} = \dfrac{44}{9}$

Finally, $|3\vec{r}|^2 = 9|\vec{r}|^2 = 9 \times \dfrac{44}{9} = 44$

Answer: $44$

questions.question: Let $\lambda \in \mathbb{Z}, \overset{→}{a} = \lambda\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{b} = 3\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$. questions.solution:
Given that

$\overset{→}{a} = \lambda\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{→}{b} = 3\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$

Also $\left(\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b} + \overset{→}{c}\right) \times \overset{→}{c} = \overset{→}{0}$

$⇒ k\left(\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b}\right) = \overset{→}{c}$

$\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{c} = - 17$ and $\overset{→}{b} \cdot \overset{→}{c} = - 20$

Now, Take $\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{c} = - 17$

$⇒ k\left(\lambda\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(\lambda\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k} + 3\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right) = - 17$

$⇒ k\left({λ}^{2} + 3\lambda + 0 - 1\right) = - 17$

$⇒ k\left({λ}^{2} + 3\lambda - 1\right) = - 17 . . . . ( 1 )$

Similarly, on taking $\overset{→}{b} \cdot \overset{→}{c} = - 20$, we get,

$k\left(3\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(\lambda\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k} + 3\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right) = - 20$

$⇒ k\left(3\lambda + 9 + 2\right) = - 20$

$⇒ k\left(3\lambda + 11\right) = - 20 . . . ( 2 )$

Now on solving equation $\left(1\right) \text{ and } \left(2\right)$ we get,

$⇒ 20{λ}^{2} + 9\lambda - 207 = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = 3, \dfrac{- 69}{20}$

For $\lambda = 3, k = - 1$

$⇒ \overset{→}{c} = - 1\left(\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b}\right)$

$⇒ - \left(\left(\lambda + 3\right)\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}\right) = - 6\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{c} \times \left(\lambda\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right) = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} \text{ and } \overset{^}{j} \text{ and } \overset{^}{k} \\ - 6 \text{ and } 0 \text{ and } - 1 \\ 3 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } 1\end{cases}\right| = \overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{c} \times \left(\lambda\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)\right|2 = 46$

Hence this is the correct option.

questions.question: Let $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}=2 \hat{i}+5 \hat{j}-\hat{k}, \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}=2 \hat{i}-2 \hat{j}+2 \hat{k}$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}$ be three vectors such that $(\vec{c}+\hat{i}) \times(\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\hat{i})=\vec{a} \times(\vec{c}+\hat{i})$. If $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c}=-29$, then $\vec{c} \cdot(-2 \hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Let's assume
$\begin{aligned}
\vec{v} & =\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\hat{i} \\
& =5 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j}+\hat{k}
\end{aligned}$
and $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}+\hat{\mathrm{i}}=\overrightarrow{\mathrm{p}}$
So,
$\begin{aligned}
& \overrightarrow{\mathrm{p}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}=\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{p}} \\
& \overrightarrow{\mathrm{p}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{p}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}=\overrightarrow{0} \\
& \overrightarrow{\mathrm{p}} \times(\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}})=\overrightarrow{0} \\
& \Rightarrow \overrightarrow{\mathrm{p}}=\lambda(\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}) \\
& \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}+\mathrm{i}=\lambda(7 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+8 \hat{\mathrm{j}}) \\
& \overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{c}}+\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \hat{\mathrm{i}}=\lambda \overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot(7 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+8 \hat{\mathrm{j}}) \\
& -29+2=\lambda(14+40) \\
& \lambda=-\frac{1}{2}
\end{aligned}$
$\begin{gathered}\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}} \cdot(-2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+\hat{\mathrm{j}}+\hat{\mathrm{k}})+\hat{\mathrm{i}} \cdot(-2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+\hat{\mathrm{j}}+\hat{\mathrm{k}})=\lambda(7 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+8 \hat{\mathrm{j}}) \cdot(-2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+\hat{\mathrm{j}}+\hat{\mathrm{k}}) \\ =-\frac{1}{2}(-14+8)+2=5\end{gathered}$

questions.q: Let $\overset{→}{a}, \overset{→}{b}, \overset{→}{c}$ be three vectors such that $\left|\overset{→}{a}\right| = \sqrt{31}, 4\left|\overset{→}{b}\right| = \left|\overset{→}{c}\right| = 2$ and $2\left(\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right) = 3\left(\overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{a}\right)$. If the angle between $\overset{→}{b}$ and $\overset{→}{c}$ is $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$, then $\left(\dfrac{\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{c}}{\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b}}\right)2$ is equal to _____ .
questions.question: Let $\overset{→}{a}, \overset{→}{b}, \overset{→}{c}$ be three vectors such that $\left|\overset{→}{a}\right| = \sqrt{31}, 4\left|\overset{→}{b}\right| = \left|\overset{→}{c}\right| = 2$ and $2\left(\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right) = 3\left(\overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{a}\right)$. If the angle between $\overset{→}{b}$ and $\overset{→}{c}$ is $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$, then $\left(\dfrac{\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{c}}{\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b}}\right)2$ is equal to _____ .
questions.solution:
Given,

$\left|\overset{→}{a}\right| = \sqrt{31}, 4\left|\overset{→}{b}\right| = \left|\overset{→}{c}\right| = 2$, $2\left(\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right) = 3\left(\overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{a}\right)$ and angle between $\overset{→}{b} \text{ and } \overset{→}{c}$ is given as $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$

Now solving, $3\left(\overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{a}\right) + 2\left(\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{a}\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(3\overset{→}{c} \times 2\overset{→}{b}\right) \times \overset{→}{a} = 0$

Means $\left(3\overset{→}{c} \times 2\overset{→}{b}\right) \text{ and } \overset{→}{a}$ are parallel vector,

So, let $3\overset{→}{c} \times 2\overset{→}{b} = \lambda\overset{→}{a}$

Now squaring both sides we get,
$9\left|\overset{→}{c}\right|2 + 4\left|\overset{→}{b}\right|2 + 12\left(\overset{→}{b} \cdot \overset{→}{c}\right) = {λ}^{2}\left|\overset{→}{a}\right|2$

$⇒ 36 + 1 + 12 \times \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2\left(cos\left(2\dfrac{π}{3}\right)\right) = {λ}^{2}\left(31\right)$

$⇒ {λ}^{2} = 1$

$⇒ \lambda = \pm 1$

Now putting the value of $\lambda$ in $\left(3\overset{→}{c} \times 2\overset{→}{b}\right) = \lambda\overset{→}{a}$ we get,

$3\overset{→}{c} + 2\overset{→}{b} = \pm \overset{→}{a} \ldots \left(1\right)$

Now taking dot product with $\overset{→}{b}$ in above equation we get,

$3\left(\overset{→}{b} \cdot \overset{→}{c}\right) + 2\left(\overset{→}{b} \cdot \overset{→}{b}\right) = \pm \overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b} = \pm \left(- \dfrac{3}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \pm \left(- 1\right)$

$⇒ \left(\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b}\right)2 = 1$

Again taking $3\left(\overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{a}\right) = 2\left(\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right)$ and sqauring both side,

$⇒ \left(\overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{a}\right)2 = \dfrac{4}{9}\left(\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right)2$

$⇒ \left(\overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{a}\right)2 = \dfrac{4}{9}\left[\left|\overset{→}{a}\right|2\left|\overset{→}{b}\right|2 - \left(\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b}\right)2\right]$

$⇒ \left(\overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{a}\right)2 = \dfrac{4}{9}\left[\dfrac{31}{4} - \left(1\right)\right]$

$⇒ \left(\overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{a}\right)2 = \dfrac{4}{9} \times \dfrac{27}{4} = 3$

Hence, the value of $\left(\dfrac{\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{c}}{\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b}}\right)2 = \dfrac{3}{1} = 3$.

questions.question: Let $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}=-\hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+2 \hat{k}, \overrightarrow{\mathrm{~b}}=8 \hat{i}+7 \hat{j}-3 \hat{k}$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}$ be vector such that $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}=\overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}$. If $\vec{c} \cdot(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})=4$, then $|\vec{a}+\vec{c}|^{2}$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
Let $\vec{c} = x\hat{i} + y\hat{j} + z\hat{k}$.
From $\vec{a} \times \vec{c} = \vec{b}$: $z - y = 4$, $z + 2x = 7$, $y + 2x = 3$.
From $\vec{c} \cdot (\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}) = 4$: $x + y + z = 4$.
Solving: $y = -1$, $z = 3$, $x = 2$.
$\vec{c} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$.
$\vec{a} + \vec{c} = (-1+2)\hat{i} + (2-1)\hat{j} + (2+3)\hat{k} = \hat{i} + \hat{j} + 5\hat{k}$.
$|\vec{a} + \vec{c}|^2 = 1 + 1 + 25 = 27$.

Then $\left|\overset{→}{c}\right|2$ is equal to _______.
questions.question: Let $\overset{→}{a} = 3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}, \overset{→}{b} = 2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{c}$ be a vector such that $\left(\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b}\right) \times \overset{→}{c} = 2\left(\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right) + 24\overset{^}{j} - 6\overset{^}{k}$ and $\left(\overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b} + \overset{^}{i}\right) . \overset{→}{c} = - 3$. Then $\left|\overset{→}{c}\right|2$ is equal to _______.
questions.solution:
Given,

$\overset{→}{a} = 3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}, \overset{→}{b} = 2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{c}$ be a vector such that $\left(\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b}\right) \times \overset{→}{c} = 2\left(\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right) + 24\overset{^}{j} - 6\overset{^}{k}$ 

Now, finding $\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} \text{ and } \overset{^}{j} \text{ and } \overset{^}{k} \\ 3 \text{ and } 2 \text{ and } 1 \\ 2 \text{ and } - 1 \text{ and } 3\end{cases}\right| = 7\overset{^}{i} - 7\overset{^}{j} - 7\overset{^}{k}$

Now, solving

$\left(\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b}\right) \times \overset{→}{c} = 2\left(\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right) + 24\overset{^}{j} - 6\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \left(5\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}\right) \times \overset{→}{c} = 2\left(7\overset{^}{i} - 7\overset{^}{j} - 7\overset{^}{k}\right) + 24\overset{^}{j} - 6\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} \text{ and } \overset{^}{j} \text{ and } \overset{^}{k} \\ 5 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } 4 \\ x \text{ and } y \text{ and } z\end{cases}\right| = 14\overset{^}{i} + 10\overset{^}{j} - 20\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \overset{^}{i}\left(z - 4y\right) - \overset{^}{j}\left(5z - 4x\right) + \overset{^}{k}\left(5y - x\right) = 14\overset{^}{i} + 10\overset{^}{j} - 20\overset{^}{k}$

Now, on comparing both side, 

$z - 4y = 14, 4x - 5z = 10, 5y - x = - 20 . . . . \left(i\right)$

Now, solving 

$\left(\overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b} + \overset{^}{i}\right) \cdot \overset{→}{c} = - 3$

$⇒ \left(2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \overset{→}{c} = - 3$

$⇒ 2x + 3y - 2z = - 3 . . . . . . . \left(ii\right)$

Now, solving the equation $\left(i\right) & \left(ii\right)$ we get,

$∴ x = 5, y = - 3, z = 2$

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{c}\right|2 = 25 + 9 + 4 = 38$

questions.solution:
Given, $\overset{→}{a} = i + j - k$ and $\overset{→}{c} = 2i - 3j + 2k$

$\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c} = \overset{→}{a}$ and $\left|\overset{→}{b}\right| \in \left\{1, 2 \ldots \ldots 10\right\}$

$∵ \overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c} = \overset{→}{a}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{a}$ is perpendicular to $\overset{→}{b}$ as well as $\overset{→}{a}$ is perpendicular to $\overset{→}{c}$ , so $\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{c} = 0$ as they are perpendicular.

Now checking $\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{c} = 2 - 3 - 2 = - 3 \ne 0$

This $\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c} = \overset{→}{a}$ is not possible.

So, number of vectors $\overset{→}{b} = 0$

questions.q: Let a vector $\overset{→}{a}$ be coplanar with vectors $\overset{→}{b} = 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{c} = \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k} .$ If $\overset{→}{a}$ is perpendicular to $\overset{→}{d} = 3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k},$ and $| \overset{→}{a} | = \sqrt{10} .$ Then a possible value of $\left[\begin{cases}\overset{→}{a}  \text{ and }  \overset{→}{b}  \text{ and }  \overset{→}{c}\end{cases}\right] + \left[\begin{cases}\overset{→}{a}  \text{ and }  \overset{→}{b}  \text{ and }  \overset{→}{d}\end{cases}\right] + \left[\begin{cases}\overset{→}{a}  \text{ and }  \overset{→}{c}  \text{ and }  \overset{→}{d}\end{cases}\right]$ is equal to:
questions.question: Let a vector $\overset{→}{a}$ be coplanar with vectors $\overset{→}{b} = 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{c} = \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k} .$ If $\overset{→}{a}$ is perpendicular to $\overset{→}{d} = 3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k},$ and $| \overset{→}{a} | = \sqrt{10} .$ Then a possible value of $\left[\begin{cases}\overset{→}{a}  \text{ and }  \overset{→}{b}  \text{ and }  \overset{→}{c}\end{cases}\right] + \left[\begin{cases}\overset{→}{a}  \text{ and }  \overset{→}{b}  \text{ and }  \overset{→}{d}\end{cases}\right] + \left[\begin{cases}\overset{→}{a}  \text{ and }  \overset{→}{c}  \text{ and }  \overset{→}{d}\end{cases}\right]$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given, a vector $\overset{→}{a}$ is coplanar with vectors $\overset{→}{b} = 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{c} = \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{a}$ is perpendicular to $\overset{→}{d} = 3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k},$ and $| \overset{→}{a} | = \sqrt{10} .$

If a vector $\overset{→}{a}$ is coplanar with the vectors $\overset{→}{b} \text{ and } \overset{→}{c}$ then it can be expressed as the linear combination of the vectors.

Thus, $\overset{→}{a} = \lambda\overset{→}{b} + \mu\overset{→}{c}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{a} = \lambda\left(2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + k\right) + \mu\left(\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + k\right)$

$⇒ \overset{→}{a} = \overset{^}{i}\left(2\lambda + \mu\right) + \overset{^}{j}\left(\lambda - \mu\right) + \overset{^}{k}\left(\lambda + \mu\right)$

Also, it is given that $\overset{→}{a}$ is perpendicular to $\overset{→}{d},$ and we know that if two vectors are perpendicular, then $\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{d} = 0$

$⇒ 3\left(2\lambda + \mu\right) + 2\left(\lambda - \mu\right) + 6\left(\lambda + \mu\right) = 0$

$⇒ 14\lambda + 7\mu = 0$

$⇒ \mu = - 2\lambda$

$⇒ \overset{→}{a} = \left(0\right)\overset{^}{i} + 3\lambda\overset{^}{j} + \left(- \lambda\right)\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{a} = \lambda\left(3\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right)$

$⇒ | \overset{→}{a} | = \sqrt{10} | \lambda |$

Given $\left|\overset{→}{a}\right| = \sqrt{10}$

$⇒ | \lambda | = 1$

$⇒ \lambda = 1$ or $- 1$

Also, if $\overset{→}{a}, \overset{→}{b} \text{ and } \overset{→}{c}$ are coplanar, then $[ \overset{→}{a}\overset{→}{b}\overset{→}{c} ] = 0$

Now, $[ \overset{→}{a}\overset{→}{b}\overset{→}{c} ] + [ \overset{→}{a}\overset{→}{b}\overset{→}{d} ] + [ \overset{→}{a}\overset{→}{c}\overset{→}{d} ]$

$= 0 + [ \overset{→}{a}\overset{→}{b}\overset{→}{d} ] + [ \overset{→}{a}\overset{→}{c}\overset{→}{d} ] = [ \overset{→}{a}\overset{→}{b} + \overset{→}{c}\overset{→}{d} ]$

On putting the values of the vectors for finding the box product, we get

$= \left|\begin{cases}0 \text{ and } 3\lambda \text{ and } - \lambda \\ 3 \text{ and } 0 \text{ and } 2 \\ 3 \text{ and } 2 \text{ and } 6\end{cases}\right|$

$= - 3\lambda ( 12 ) - \lambda ( 6 ) = - 42\lambda = - 42$ or $42 .$

questions.q: Let $\overset{→}{x}$ be a vector in the plane containing vectors $\overset{→}{a} = 2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{b} = \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k} .$ If the vector $\overset{→}{x}$ is perpendicular to $( 3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k} )$ and its projection on $\overset{→}{a}$ is $\dfrac{17\sqrt{6}}{2},$ then the value of $\left|\overset{→}{x}\right|2$ is equal to _______.
questions.question: Let $\overset{→}{x}$ be a vector in the plane containing vectors $\overset{→}{a} = 2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{b} = \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k} .$ If the vector $\overset{→}{x}$ is perpendicular to $( 3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k} )$ and its projection on $\overset{→}{a}$ is $\dfrac{17\sqrt{6}}{2},$ then the value of $\left|\overset{→}{x}\right|2$ is equal to _______.
questions.solution:
A plane containing two vectors can be expressed as a linear combination of the vectors.

Hence, let $\overset{→}{x} = \lambda\overset{→}{a} + \mu\overset{→}{b} ( \lambda$ and $\mu$ are scalars$) .$

$⇒ \overset{→}{x} = \overset{^}{i} ( 2\lambda + \mu ) + \overset{^}{j} ( 2\mu - \lambda ) + \overset{^}{k} ( \lambda - \mu )$

Since $\overset{→}{x}$ is perpendicular to $3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k},$

$⇒ \overset{→}{x} \cdot \left(3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(\overset{^}{i} ( 2\lambda + \mu ) + \overset{^}{j} ( 2\mu - \lambda ) + \overset{^}{k} ( \lambda - \mu )\right) \cdot \left(3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right) = 0$

$⇒ 3 ( 2\lambda + \mu ) + 2 ( 2\mu - \lambda ) - ( \lambda - \mu ) = 0$

$⇒ 3\lambda + 8\mu = 0 . . . \left(1\right)$

Also, the projection of $\overset{→}{x}$ on $\overset{→}{a}$ is $\dfrac{17\sqrt{6}}{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\overset{→}{x} \cdot \overset{→}{a}}{| \overset{→}{a} |} = \dfrac{17\sqrt{6}}{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(\overset{^}{i} ( 2\lambda + \mu ) + \overset{^}{j} ( 2\mu - \lambda ) + \overset{^}{k} ( \lambda - \mu )\right) \cdot \left(2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)}{{2}^{2} + {1}^{2} + {1}^{2}} = \dfrac{17\sqrt{6}}{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{2 ( 2\lambda + \mu ) - ( 2\mu - \lambda ) + ( \lambda - \mu )}{6} = \dfrac{17\sqrt{6}}{2}$

$⇒ 6\lambda - \mu = 51 . . . \left(2\right)$

On solving the equations $( 1 )$ and $( 2 ) ,$ we get $\lambda = 8, \mu = - 3 .$

Thus, $\overset{→}{x} = 13\overset{^}{i} - 14\overset{^}{j} + 11\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{x}\right| = \sqrt{{13}^{2} + \left(- 14\right)2 + {11}^{2}}$

$⇒ | \overset{→}{x}{|}^{2} = 486 .$

questions.question: Let ${x}_{0}$ be the point of local maxima of  $f\left(x\right) = \overset{→}{a} \cdot \left(\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c}\right),$ where$\overset{→}{a} = x\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}, \overset{→}{b} = - 2\overset{^}{i} + x\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{c} = 7\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + x\overset{^}{k} .$ Then the value of $\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b} + \overset{→}{b} \cdot \overset{→}{c} + \overset{→}{c} \cdot \overset{→}{a}$ at $x = {x}_{0}$ is:

$f\left(x\right) = \left[\overset{→}{a}\overset{→}{b}\overset{→}{c}\right] = \left|\begin{array}{ll}x - 23 \\ - 2x - 1 \\ 7 - 2x\end{array}\right|$

$= x\left({x}^{2} - 2\right) + 2\left(- 2x + 7\right) + 3\left(4 - 7x\right)$

$= {x}^{3} - 2x - 4x + 14 + 12 - 21x$

$f\left(x\right) = {x}^{3} - 27x + 26$

$f ' \left(x\right) = 3{x}^{2} - 27 = 3\left(x - 3\right)\left(x + 3\right)$

so local maxima point is ${x}_{0} = - 3$

Now $\overset{→}{a} . \overset{→}{b} + \overset{→}{b} . \overset{→}{c} + \overset{→}{c} . \overset{→}{a} = - 2x - 2x - 3 - 14 - 2x - x + 7x + 4 + 3x = 3x - 13$

at $x = {x}_{0} = - 3$

$\overset{→}{a} . \overset{→}{b} + \overset{→}{b} . \overset{→}{c} + \overset{→}{c} . \overset{→}{a} = - 9 - 13 = - 22$

If the minimum value of the scalar triple product $\left[\overset{→}{u}\overset{→}{v}\overset{→}{w}\right]$ is $- \alpha\sqrt{3401}$, and $\left|\overset{→}{u} . \overset{^}{i}\right|2 = \dfrac{m}{n}$ where $m$ and $n$ are coprime natural numbers, then $m + n$ is equal to _____ .
questions.question: Let $\overset{→}{v} = \alpha\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}, \overset{→}{w} = 2\alpha\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$, and $\overset{→}{u}$ be a vector such that $\left|\overset{→}{u}\right| = \alpha > 0$. If the minimum value of the scalar triple product $\left[\overset{→}{u}\overset{→}{v}\overset{→}{w}\right]$ is $- \alpha\sqrt{3401}$, and $\left|\overset{→}{u} . \overset{^}{i}\right|2 = \dfrac{m}{n}$ where $m$ and $n$ are coprime natural numbers, then $m + n$ is equal to _____ .
questions.solution:
We have,

$\left[\overset{→}{u}\overset{→}{v}\overset{→}{w}\right] = \overset{→}{u} \cdot \left(\overset{→}{v} \times \overset{→}{w}\right)$

Now,

$min\left(\left[\overset{→}{u}\overset{→}{v}\overset{→}{w}\right]\right) = - \alpha\sqrt{3401}$

$⇒ - \left|\overset{→}{u}\right|\left|\overset{→}{v} \times \overset{→}{w}\right| = - \alpha\sqrt{3401}$

If $\overset{→}{d}$ be a vector such that $\overset{→}{b} \cdot \overset{→}{d} = \overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b}$, then $( \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} ) \cdot ( \overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{d} )$ is equal to
questions.question: Let $\overset{→}{a}, \overset{→}{b}$ and $\overset{→}{c}$ be three non zero vectors such that $\overset{→}{b} \cdot \overset{→}{c} = 0$ and $\overset{→}{a} \times ( \overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c} ) = \dfrac{\overset{→}{b} - \overset{→}{c}}{2}$. If $\overset{→}{d}$ be a vector such that $\overset{→}{b} \cdot \overset{→}{d} = \overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b}$, then $( \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} ) \cdot ( \overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{d} )$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given,

$\overset{→}{a} \times \left(\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c}\right) = \dfrac{\overset{→}{b} - \overset{→}{c}}{2}$

Using the vector triple cross product we have,

$\overset{→}{a} \times \left(\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c}\right) = \left(\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{c}\right)\overset{→}{b} - \left(\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b}\right)\overset{→}{c}$

So, $( \overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{c} ) \overset{→}{b} - ( \overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b} ) \overset{→}{c} = \dfrac{\overset{→}{b} - \overset{→}{c}}{2}$

On comparing both sides we get,

$\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{c} = \dfrac{1}{2}, \overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$∵ \overset{→}{b} \cdot \overset{→}{d} = \overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b}$

$∴ \overset{→}{b} \cdot \overset{→}{d} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Using vector cross-product formulae we have

$( \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} ) \cdot ( \overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{d} ) = \overset{→}{a} \cdot ( \overset{→}{b} \times ( \overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{d} ) )$

$= \overset{→}{a} \cdot ( ( \overset{→}{b} \cdot \overset{→}{d} ) \overset{→}{c} - ( \overset{→}{b} \cdot \overset{→}{c} ) \overset{→}{d} )$ $\left(∵ \overset{→}{b} \cdot \overset{→}{c} = 0\right)$

$= ( \overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{c} ) ( \overset{→}{b} \cdot \overset{→}{d} ) = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{1}{4}$

questions.solution:
Given,

$\overset{→}{a} = \lambda\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{→}{b} = \overset{^}{i} - \lambda\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$

Also given,

$( ( \overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b} ) \times ( \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} ) ) \times ( \overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b} ) = 8\overset{^}{i} - 40\overset{^}{j} - 24\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ ( \overset{→}{b} - \overset{→}{a} ) \times ( ( \overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b} ) \times ( \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} ) ) = 8\overset{^}{i} - 40\overset{^}{j} - 24\overset{^}{k}$

Now using vector triple product,

$\overset{→}{A} \times ( \overset{→}{B} \times \overset{→}{C} ) = ( \overset{→}{A} . \overset{→}{C} ) \overset{→}{B} - ( \overset{→}{A} . \overset{→}{B} ) \overset{→}{C}$ we get,

$⇒ ( ( \overset{→}{b} - \overset{→}{a} ) \cdot ( \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} ) ) ( \overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b} ) - ( ( \overset{→}{b} - \overset{→}{a} ) \cdot ( \overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b} ) ) ( \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} ) = 8\overset{^}{i} - 40\overset{^}{j} - 24\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ 0 + ( ( \overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b} ) \cdot ( \overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b} ) ) ( \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} ) = 8\overset{^}{i} - 40\overset{^}{j} - 24\overset{^}{k} . . . . . ( 1 )$

$( ( \overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b} ) \cdot ( \overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b} ) ) = \left[\left(\lambda - 1\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(2 + \lambda\right)\overset{^}{j} - 5\overset{^}{k}\right] . \left[\left(\lambda + 1\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(2 - \lambda\right)\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right]$

$⇒ ( ( \overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b} ) \cdot ( \overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b} ) ) = 8$

From equation (1) we get,

$⇒ 8 ( \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} ) = 8\overset{^}{i} - 40\overset{^}{j} - 24\overset{^}{k}$

Now, $\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} \text{ and } \overset{^}{j} \text{ and } \overset{^}{k} \\ \lambda \text{ and } 2 \text{ and } - 3 \\ 1 \text{ and } - \lambda \text{ and } 2\end{cases}\right|$

$= ( 4 - 3\lambda ) \overset{^}{i} - ( 2\lambda + 3 ) \overset{^}{j} + \left(- {λ}^{2} - 2\right)\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \lambda = 1$

$∴ \overset{→}{a} = \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{→}{b} = \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b} = 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}, \overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b} = 3\overset{^}{j} - 5\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ ( \overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b} ) \times ( \overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b} ) = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} \text{ and } \overset{^}{j} \text{ and } \overset{^}{k} \\ 2 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } - 1 \\ 0 \text{ and } 3 \text{ and } - 5\end{cases}\right| = 2\overset{^}{i} + 10\overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \left|( \overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b} ) \times ( \overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b} )\right| = \sqrt{4 + 100 + 36}$

Now,

$\left|\lambda ( \overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b} ) \times ( \overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b} )\right|2 = {λ}^{2}\left|( \overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b} ) \times ( \overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b} )\right|2$

$∴$ Required answer $= 4 + 100 + 36 = 140$

questions.question: Let $\overset{→}{a} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{b} = - \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k} .$ Then the vector product $\left(\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b}\right) \times \left(\left(\overset{→}{a} \times \left(\left(\overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b}\right) \times \overset{→}{b}\right)\right) \times \overset{→}{b}\right)$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
$\overset{→}{a} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{→}{b} = - \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b} = 3\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}; \overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b} = - 1 + 2 + 6 = 7$

Now $\left(\left(\overset{→}{a} \times \left(\left(\overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b}\right) \times \overset{→}{b}\right)\right) \times \overset{→}{b}\right)$

$= \left(\left(\overset{→}{a} \times \left(\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} - \overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{b}\right)\right) \times \overset{→}{b}\right)$

$= \left(\overset{→}{a} \times \left(\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} - 0\right)\right) \times \overset{→}{b}$

$= \left(\overset{→}{a} \times \left(\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right)\right) \times \overset{→}{b}$

$= \left(\left(\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b}\right)\overset{→}{a} - \left(\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{a}\right)\overset{→}{b}\right) \times \overset{→}{b}$

$= \left(\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b}\right)\left(\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right) - \left(\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{a}\right)\left(\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{b}\right)$

$= \left(\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b}\right)\left(\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right)$

Here, $\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} \text{ and } \overset{^}{j} \text{ and } \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } 2 \\ - 1 \text{ and } 2 \text{ and } 3\end{cases}\right| = - \overset{^}{i} - 5\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$

$∴ \left(\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b}\right)\left(\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right) = 7\left(- \overset{^}{i} - 5\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right)$

So, $\left(\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b}\right) \times \left(7\left(- \overset{^}{i} - 5\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right)\right)$

$7\left(0\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}\right) \times \left(- \overset{^}{i} - 5\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right)$

questions.solution:
Given: $\overset{→}{a} + 5\overset{→}{b}$ is collinear with $\overset{→}{c}, \overset{→}{b} + 6\overset{→}{c}$ is collinear with $\overset{→}{a}$ and $\overset{→}{a} + \alpha\overset{→}{b} + \beta\overset{→}{c} = \overset{→}{0}$.

$⇒ \overset{→}{a} + 5\overset{→}{b} = \lambda\overset{→}{c} . . . \left(i\right)$

$⇒ \overset{→}{b} + 6\overset{→}{c} = \mu\overset{→}{a} . . . \left(ii\right)$

$⇒ \overset{→}{a} = \lambda\overset{→}{c} - 5\overset{→}{b} = \dfrac{\overset{→}{b} + 6\overset{→}{c}}{μ}$

$⇒ \lambda\overset{→}{c} - 5\overset{→}{b} = \dfrac{6}{μ}\overset{→}{c} + \dfrac{1}{μ}\overset{→}{b}$

Comparing both the sides,

$⇒ \mu = \dfrac{- 1}{5}, \lambda = - 30$

Putting these values in equation $\left(i\right)$

$⇒ \overset{→}{a} + 5\overset{→}{b} = - 30\overset{→}{c}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{a} + 5\overset{→}{b} + 30\overset{→}{c} = 0$

Comparing this equation with $\overset{→}{a} + \alpha\overset{→}{b} + \beta\overset{→}{c} = \overset{→}{0}$.

$⇒ \alpha = 5, \beta = 30$

$⇒ \alpha + \beta = 35$

questions.question: Let the position vectors of the points $A, B, C$ and $D$ be $5\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j} + 2\lambda\overset{^}{k}, \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}, - 2\overset{^}{i} + \lambda\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$ and $- \overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k} .$ Let the set $S = { \lambda \in \mathbb{R}:$ the points $A, B, C$ and $D$ are coplanar$} .$ The $\mathop{∑}_{\lambda \in S} ( \lambda + 2{)}^{2}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given that:

$A ( 5, 5, 2\lambda )$, $B\left(1, 2, 3\right)$, $C\left(- 2, \lambda, 4\right)$ and

$D\left(- 1, 5, 6\right)$.

Now,

$\overset{→}{AB} ≡ ( - 4, - 3, 3 - 2\lambda )$

$\overset{→}{AC} ≡ ( - 7, \lambda - 5, 4 - 2\lambda )$

$\overset{→}{AD} ≡ ( - 6, 0, 6 - 2\lambda )$

Given that $A, B, C\text{and}D$ are coplanar.

$∴ [ \overset{→}{AB}\overset{→}{AC}\overset{→}{AD} ] = 0$

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}- 4 \text{ and } - 3 \text{ and } 3 - 2\lambda \\ - 7 \text{ and } \lambda - 5 \text{ and } 4 - 2\lambda \\ - 6 \text{ and } 0 \text{ and } 6 - 2\lambda\end{cases}\right| = 0$

Expand the determinant along the first row.

$⇒ - 4\left[\left(\lambda - 5\right)\left(6 - 2\lambda\right) - 0\right] - \left(- 3\right)\left[- 7\left(6 - 2\lambda\right) - \left(- 6\right)\left(4 - 2\lambda\right)\right] + \left(3 - 2\lambda\right)\left[0 - \left(- 6\right)\left(\lambda - 5\right)\right]$

On solving the above equation we get,

$∴ \lambda = 3, \lambda = 2$

We have two values of $\lambda$.

$⇒ \mathop{∑}_{\lambda \in s} ( \lambda + 2{)}^{2} = \left(3 + 2\right)2 + \left(2 + 2\right)2$

$= 41$

Hence, $\mathop{∑}_{\lambda \in s} ( \lambda + 2{)}^{2} = 41$

questions.question: Let the vectors $\overset{→}{u1} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + a\overset{^}{k}, \overset{→}{u2} = \overset{^}{i} + b\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k},$ and $\overset{→}{u3} = c\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ be coplanar. If the vectors $\overset{→}{v1} = \left(a + b\right)\overset{^}{i} + c\overset{^}{j} + c\overset{^}{k}, \overset{→}{v2} = a\overset{^}{i} + \left(b + c\right)\overset{^}{j} + a\overset{^}{k}$ and  $\overset{→}{v}3 = b\overset{^}{i} + b\overset{^}{j} + \left(c + a\right)\overset{^}{k}$ are also coplanar, then $6\left(a + b + c\right)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given: $\overset{→}{u}1 = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + a\overset{^}{k}, \overset{→}{u}2 = \overset{^}{i} + b\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{u}3 = c\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ are coplanar.

Also given that,$\overset{→}{v}1 = \left(a + b\right)\overset{^}{i} + c\overset{^}{j} + c\overset{^}{k}, \overset{→}{v}2 = a\overset{^}{i} + \left(b + c\right)\overset{^}{j} + a\overset{^}{k}$and $\overset{→}{v}3 = b\overset{^}{i} + b\overset{^}{j} + \left(c + a\right)\overset{^}{k}$ are coplanar.

Now, using the condition of coplanar we get,

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}1 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } a \\ 1 \text{ and } b \text{ and } 1 \\ c \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } 1\end{cases}\right| = 0$

Expanding the determinant along ${R}_{1}$.

$⇒ \left(b - 1\right) - \left(1 - c\right) + a\left(1 - bc\right) = 0$

$⇒ a + b + c = 2 + abc . . . . . \left(i\right)$

Again using the coplanar condition we get,

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}a + b \text{ and } c \text{ and } c \\ a \text{ and } b + c \text{ and } a \\ b \text{ and } b \text{ and } c + a\end{cases}\right| = 0$

Apply row transformations, $\left({R}_{3} \to {R}_{3} - \left({R}_{1} + {R}_{2}\right)\right)$

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}a + b \text{ and } c \text{ and } c \\ a \text{ and } b + c \text{ and } a \\ - 2a \text{ and } - 2c \text{ and } 0\end{cases}\right| = 0$

Expand the determinant along ${R}_{1}$.

$⇒ \left(a + b\right)\left(0 + 2ac\right) - c\left(0 + 2{a}^{2}\right) + c\left(- 2ac + 2a\left(b + c\right)\right) = 0$

$⇒ 2{a}^{2}c + 2abc - 2{a}^{2}c - 2a{c}^{2} + 2abc + 2a{c}^{2} = 0$

$⇒ abc = 0$

$∴ a + b + c = 2$ (From eq $\left(i\right)$)

$∴ 6\left(a + b + c\right) = 12$

Hence this is the correct option.

questions.solution:
The given equations are coplanar.

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}\lambda \text{ and } - 1 \text{ and } 1 \\ 1 \text{ and } 2 \text{ and } \mu \\ 3 \text{ and } - 4 \text{ and } 5\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ \lambda\left[10 + 4\mu\right] + 1\left[5 - 3\mu\right] + 1\left[- 10\right] = 0$

$⇒ 4\lambda\mu + 10\lambda - 3\mu = 5 . . . . . . . \left(i\right)$

And $\lambda - \mu = 5$

So, by $\left(1\right)$

$⇒ 4\left(5 + \mu\right)\mu + 10\left(5 + \mu\right) - 3\mu = 5$

$⇒ 4{μ}^{2} + 27\mu + 45 = 0$

$⇒ 4{μ}^{2} + 15\mu + 12\mu + 45 = 0$

$∴ \mu = - 3, \dfrac{- 15}{4}$

$⇒ \lambda = 2, \dfrac{5}{4}$

$∴ \mathop{∑}_{\lambda\mu \in S}80\left({λ}^{2} + {μ}^{2}\right) = 80\left[\left(9 + 4\right) + \dfrac{225}{16} + \dfrac{25}{16}\right]$

$= 80\left[13 + \dfrac{125}{8}\right] = 10 \times 229$

$= 2290$

Hence this is the correct option.

questions.question: Let $\alpha \beta \gamma=45 ; \alpha, \beta, \gamma \in \mathbb{R}$. If $x(\alpha, 1,2)+y(1, \beta, 2)+z(2,3, \gamma)=(0,0,0)$ for some $x, y, z \in \mathbb{R}, x y z \neq 0$, then $6 \alpha+4 \beta+\gamma$ is equal to _______
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \alpha \beta \gamma=45, \alpha \beta \gamma \in \mathrm{R} \\ & \mathrm{x}(\alpha, 1,2)+\mathrm{y}(1, \beta, 2)+\mathrm{z}(2,3, \gamma)=(0,0,0) \\ & \mathrm{x}, \mathrm{y}, \mathrm{z} \in \mathrm{R}, \mathrm{xyz} \neq 0 \\ & \alpha \mathrm{x}+\mathrm{y}+2 \mathrm{z}=0 \\ & \mathrm{x}+\beta \mathrm{y}+3 \mathrm{z}=0 \\ & 2 \mathrm{x}+2 \mathrm{y}+\gamma \mathrm{z}=0 \\ & \mathrm{xyz} \neq 0 \Rightarrow \text { non-trivial } \\ & \left|\begin{array}{lll}\alpha & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & \beta & 3 \\ 2 & 2 & \gamma\end{array}\right|=0\end{aligned}$
